chunks: As-Sayyid ar-Radi says: I say: His (peace be upon him) word 'mutadhā'ib'
means 'muḍṭarib' (i.e. moved or troubled), as they say 'tadhā'abat ar-rīḥ' (i.e. the winds blow in troubled manner), and from this the wolf was named 'dhi'b', because of its troubled movement.
ai.seo_question: What is the linguistic meaning of 'mutadhā'ib' in Nahj al-Balagha and its etymological connection to the wolf?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi elucidates the term 'mutadhā'ib' as denoting agitation or turbulence, drawing a vivid linguistic parallel between the erratic movement of the wind and the distinctive, unsettled gait of a wolf. This etymological analysis underscores the physical manifestation of inner cowardice and instability in those who shrink from battle, a key theme in the sermons of Imam Ali (peace be upon him).

en.sayed-ali-raza: as-Sayyid ar-Raḍī says: Amīr al-mu’minīn’s word “mutadhā‘ib”
means “muḍṭarib” (i.e. moved or troubled), as they say “tadhā‘abat ar-rīḥ” (i.e. the winds blow in troubled manner). Similarly the wolf is called “dhi‘b” because of its trouble movement.
